column1: # The stand's own run parameters, in ONE declared place (X19 S11).
# Before this, `--freeze-before` hardcoded the "before" commit as a string
# literal, and the axis list `A,B,D` was written TWICE inside
# scripts/promise-effect.php — once as the default for `--axis=`, once more
# as the fixed iteration order of the summary loops. A round that changed one
# without the other would silently stop measuring an axis. Both now come from
# this file, read once at startup.
# `before-commit` is not just compared against HEAD: a value that is not a
# real commit in this repository refuses the run before anything else runs,
# so a typo here cannot silently defeat the very check it exists to make (the
# X18 lesson of a guard whose constants named paths that did not exist, and
# so could never redden).
# `axes` lists every axis the grid spans, in the fixed order the summary is
# printed in. `--axis=` narrows a run against this same list; it never
# replaces it. It is also held against the script's own generator map in both
# directions: a declared axis nothing produces, and a generator nothing
# declares, are two ways of not measuring in silence.
# `blocking-axes` names the subset whose defects move the EXIT CODE. It is a
# decision of the round and not a property of an axis, which is why it is
# declared rather than written into the summary loop:
#   A, D  cured by this programme, so a defect blocks;
#   C, E  cured now too, so they block from X20 on. C's one mechanism is
#         repaired and E stands at zero; the reason they were excluded — a
#         stage that must produce their grid cannot also demand it be green —
#         expired with the round that produced them. Four floor rows are not a
#         substitute for an exit code.
#   B     81 cells over four mechanisms, and what a top-level shorthand MEANS
#         beside the nested block it is shorthand for is one undecided
#         question, taken whole by the round that owns it. The earlier reason
#         recorded here — that the rule layer has no notion of "channel
#         boundary", citing `channel-identity-substrate.md` — does not survive
#         reading that document: it is about finding identity across
#         suppression, threshold, selector and exclusion consumers and never
#         mentions this axis, pairs or coexistence. X17's actual recorded
#         reason was that no owner held a mandate over pair semantics.
# WHAT A BLOCKING AXIS IS WORTH, so the word is not read as more than it is:
# nothing automatic consumes this script's exit code. `composer check` reaches
# the stand only through `promise-effect:grid:check`, which compares the
# committed artifact against its declarations and takes no probe of its own,
# and no workflow runs the stand. A blocking axis is therefore protected at a
# round's own validation step and nowhere else. Automating it would put a
# ~200-second run into `composer check`, against roughly 150 seconds for the
# whole test suite; that is the number, and X20 did not spend it.
key
before-commit
axes
blocking-axes
